title: Introduce bootstrapped presubmit Docker image and dependency-harvest job
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Add hermetic presubmit image and automated dependency harvesting job to reduce CI flakiness and shrink presubmit setup time.
description:
Summary: This PR introduces a small, bootstrapped Docker image for presubmit jobs and an automated dependency-harvest step that periodically scans transitive deps to produce a curated shrinkwrap used by CI.
Motivation: presubmit latency and network-dependent install steps are a major contributor to flaky CI and long feedback loops; shrinking the runtime, baking toolchain artifacts into an image, and proactively harvesting transitive deps will make CI faster and more deterministic.
What changed: 1) docker/ci/presubmit.Dockerfile — new minimal build image anchored on distroless with pinned packaging binaries and cached wheels for critical toolchain packages; 2) .github/workflows/presubmit.yml — split presubmit into fast and slow lanes and use the new image; 3) tools/dep_harvest/harvest.py & scripts/dep-harvest.sh — new lightweight harvester that runs weekly, emits a shrinkwrap JSON, and creates a dep-bump PR to vendor-critical toolchain artifacts; 4) tools/ci/entrypoint.go — small adaptor to assert environment invariants and pre-warm TLS and pip caches; 5) docs/dev/presubmit.md — onboarding notes and emergency rollback instructions.
Checklist: - [x] Validate new image boots in local dev - [x] Smoke-presubmit passes with image pinned - [x] Harvest job emits reproducible shrinkwrap - [x] Rollout plan documented in presubmit.md - [x] Security review for added binaries completed
Commits summary: "bootstrap presubmit image with distroless base and pinned toolchain"; "add dep harvester and weekly workflow"; "adapt presubmit workflow to use new image and fast/slow lanes"; "docs: presubmit onboarding and rollback".
Changed files (high-level): docker/ci/presubmit.Dockerfile; .github/workflows/presubmit.yml; tools/dep_harvest/harvest.py; scripts/dep-harvest.sh; tools/ci/entrypoint.go; docs/dev/presubmit.md; Makefile (ci targets); .dockerignore; tests/presubmit/smoke_test.sh.
Review thread highlights: Reviewer Ethan Park: "Nice approach — can we avoid bundling curl/apt into the image to reduce attack surface?" Author reply: "Removed apt/curl; switched to multi-stage build to package only essential binaries and use distroless runtime". Reviewer Lena Müller: "Harvest produces a large shrinkwrap; how do we avoid bloating repo history?" Author reply: "Harvest emits shrinkwrap into artifacts storage and creates a PR that vendors only a minimal subset; presubmit reads the artifact by URL; we added retention policy in docs." Reviewer Samir Rao (security): "Please add SBOM and attestation; confirm reproducible build inputs." Author reply: "Added SBOM generation step and documented deterministic build inputs; CI asserts checksum on image build." 
CI summary: initial run failed on lint (missing gofmt fix), author pushed fix; subsequent pipeline passed full presubmit matrix including unit, lint, image-build, dep-harvest dry-run, and smoke e2e.
Rollout and merge: canary enabled on git refs from core-team and opt-in for customer-facing repos for 48h, then global.
Merge note: squashed into one commit; merged after two approvals and green CI.
Impact: presubmit median startup time reduced ~45%, flakiness on network installs dropped by ~82% in two-week pilot.
Risk & rollback: image is tagged with content-based tag; to rollback, change presubmit workflow to use the previous pinned tag and revert the harvest workflow schedule.
Related: ENG-5421, DEV-217, SUP-4219.

notes: This PR focuses on reducing CI variance by moving runtime dependencies into an immutable image and proactively harvesting transitive dependencies. The dep-harvest job is intentionally conservative: it opens a draft PR that owners can opt into. The new presubmit image reduces external network fetches and speeds up environment setup. Monitoring dashboards were added under Redwood Console -> CI Observability to track presubmit startup percentiles and harvest PR churn.
